habitat-global-village-ahuachapan-el-sal.about:
Global Village is Habitat for Humanity's week-long international volunteer programme. This open build in Ahuachapán, El Salvador runs 13 March 2027 – 20 March 2027 (home construction). Part of the Building Hope project: volunteers help construct reinforced concrete-block homes for 36 families and improve homes for 24 more in western El Salvador.

Individual volunteers can join on their own or with friends; teams of 12–24 people are led by an experienced Habitat team leader. A typical itinerary is arrival day, a cultural or learning exchange, four build days working alongside a local contractor, families and community volunteers, a visit to other Habitat projects and a farewell, then departure. No construction or language skills are needed.

Costs: a programme donation of US$2,125 supports Habitat's housing work and covers your shared hotel room, meals and ground transport on site. International flights, travel insurance and visas are extra. Many volunteers fundraise the donation. Adults 18+ only (this build does not accept volunteers under 18).
highlights: One-week home construction build in Ahuachapán, El Salvador (13 March 2027 – 20 March 2027)
Programme donation US$2,125 covers accommodation, meals and local transport; flights extra
Run by Habitat for Humanity, a major international housing non-profit; no skills required
habitat-global-village-ahuachapan-el-sal.eligibility: Open to individuals of any nationality who can obtain the necessary visa and are in good physical health (work can be strenuous). Adults 18+ only (this build does not accept volunteers under 18).

habsmun-2027.about:
HabsMUN is a THIMUN-affiliated conference, now in its 19th year, hosted by Haberdashers' Elstree Schools just outside London. It opens on Friday night with an opening ceremony and lobbying, followed by two days of debate.

The conference runs 12–14 March 2027 at Haberdashers' Elstree Schools (north-west of London), United Kingdom. It is open to secondary school students in school delegations. Working language: English.

Schools register through the official site after reading the invitation letter. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 12–14 March 2027 in Elstree, United Kingdom
THIMUN-affiliated, THIMUN rules of procedure
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
habsmun-2027.eligibility: Open to secondary school students in school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Schools register through the official site after reading the invitation letter.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
habsmun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

harvard-model-congress-boston-2027.about:
Harvard Model Congress is the largest congressional simulation conference in the world, run by Harvard undergraduates for 42 years. Instead of the UN, students role-play US senators, representatives, cabinet members, journalists and justices.

The conference runs 18–21 February 2027 at Boston, United States. It is open to high school students. Working language: English.

Schools and delegates register through the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

World's largest congressional simulation
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page

hcssim-2027.about:
HCSSiM has run since 1971 and immerses talented and highly motivated high-school students in university-level mathematics for six weeks: morning workshops on proofs and problem solving, afternoon problem sessions, evening maxi- and mini-courses and a close-knit residential community. Many alumni became research mathematicians.

In 2026 it ran 28 June – 8 August on the Hampshire College campus. Hampshire College is closing, but HCSSiM continues as an independent organisation and will announce its 2027 campus in late 2026. Applicants submit an application and the 'Interesting Test', a set of puzzles that shows how you think.
highlights: Proof-based workshops that teach how mathematicians actually work
Admission puzzle ('Interesting Test') rather than grades
Ample need-based financial aid
hcssim-2027.eligibility: Talented, highly motivated high-school students. The page does not restrict nationality; international applicants should check visa and travel logistics.
how_to_apply: Check hcssim.org in late 2026 for the 2027 campus and dates
Download and work on the Interesting Test
Submit the online application (deadline mid-April in 2026)
Submit the Interesting Test about a week later
Apply for financial aid via hcssim.org/money if needed
hcssim-2027.costs: 2026 fee USD 7,208 (tuition, room and board). Ample need-based aid available.

henhacks-2027.about:
HenHacks 2027 is the University of Delaware's hackathon. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at University of Delaware in Newark, DE from 2027-03-06 to 2027-03-07. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Free entry, food and mentoring
Official MLH 2027 season event
Build a portfolio project in one weekend
henhacks-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://www.henhackshackathon.com/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
henhacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

hiamun-2027.about:
HIAMUN is the Model United Nations conference of HAYAH International Academy in New Cairo and has been running for 17 years as a THIMUN-affiliated event. HIAMUN '27 takes place on 21–24 January 2027 with the theme 'Convergence'. Forums include GA1, GA3, GA4, GA6, UNCAC, the Human Rights Council, CCPCJ, the Arab League, ECOSOC, the Security Council and the ICJ.

It is for secondary-school students, usually attending as school delegations; the conference also has a charity focus (organisers report raising more than EGP 950,000 over the years).

One of Egypt's most established school MUNs and a good THIMUN-style experience in the region.
highlights: THIMUN-affiliated, 17-year history
Wide range of forums including Arab League and ICJ
Charity-driven conference culture
hiamun-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students, usually through their school MUN club. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Read the forums on hiamun.org
Ask your MUN director to contact mun@hayahacademy.com to register the school
Receive country allocations and research reports
Attend 21–24 January 2027
hiamun-2027.costs: Delegate and school fees are sent to registered schools; travel and accommodation extra.

himcm-2026.about:
The High School Mathematical Contest in Modeling (HiMCM) is run by COMAP. Teams of up to four students, with a faculty advisor, choose one of the released problems and have any consecutive 14 days within the window to research, model and submit a solution paper.

Papers are judged on assumptions, modelling, analysis and clarity, and graded Outstanding, Finalist, Meritorious, Honorable Mention or Successful Participant. It is excellent preparation for the MCM/ICM and IMMC and looks strong on applications for maths, economics and engineering.
highlights: Teams of up to 4 with an advisor
Real-world open problems
Any 14 days inside 4–17 November
himcm-2026.eligibility: Students in high-school grades or below, from any country; teams need a teacher/faculty advisor who registers them.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to act as advisor
Advisor registers the team on contest.comap.com and pays the fee
Choose a problem when released and work for your chosen period
Submit the solution paper before the window closes
himcm-2026.costs: Team registration fee paid by the advisor (see COMAP site).

hive-helsinki-tuition-free-coding-school.about:
Hive Helsinki is the Helsinki campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). Hive's selection is called a check-in; the next on-campus check-in information session listed is 12 November 2026, and the studies last 18 months full-time. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.
highlights: 100% tuition-free, peer-to-peer, project-based learning
No diploma or coding experience needed; 18+
Part of the global 42 Network (50+ campuses)
hive-helsinki-tuition-free-coding-school.eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or over, any nationality, no diploma or prior coding required. Non-residents need the right to stay in Finland for the Piscine and studies. Working language: English.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the campus website and take the online logic test.
Book an introduction/check-in meeting.
Choose and attend a four-week on-site Piscine.
If selected, start the core curriculum.
hive-helsinki-tuition-free-coding-school.costs: Tuition-free. Housing, food, travel and visa costs are the student's own.

hive-young-writers-competition-2027.about:
Hive's competition has three age categories (14–16, 17–19, 20–30) and no set theme. Writers may enter up to two pieces of any form — poetry, flash fiction or stories (including script style) — and individual and class entries are welcome.

Prizes include print publication, professional feedback and mentoring sessions, and tech and writing prizes; commended writers are invited to submit to the next Hive anthology.
highlights: Free; three age categories
Poetry, flash fiction and stories
Mentoring and publication prizes
hive-young-writers-competition-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 14–30 living in, from or studying in the North or Midlands of England (as defined on Hive's map).
how_to_apply: Check you are in the eligible region (map on the site)
Write up to two pieces
Enter online before midnight on 24 Feb 2027

hku-summer-institute-2027.about:
HKUSI offers a menu of summer programmes taught by HKU faculty: for secondary students (for example Technopreneurship with the HKU School of Innovation, a Chemistry Summer School, research-skills programmes) and for undergraduates/postgraduates (for example International Business in Practice with HKU Business School, Governance and Policy Leadership). Students live in HKU residences and join enrichment events across Hong Kong.

The 2027 line-up and deadlines will be published on the HKUSI site; programmes usually open for applications in winter and spring.
highlights: Programmes co-designed with HKU faculties
Options for secondary, undergraduate and postgraduate students
Residential experience in Hong Kong
hku-summer-institute-2027.eligibility: Secondary students (typically grades 10–12) and university students from any country, depending on the programme. Good English required.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to HKUSI updates and check the 2027 programme list
Choose a programme for your level
Apply via the HKUSI application system
Pay fees and arrange travel once admitted
hku-summer-institute-2027.costs: Paid programmes; fees and accommodation costs listed per programme on the HKUSI site.

hkusi-winter-chapter-shanghai-2027.about:
The HKU Summer Institute (HKUSI) runs short immersive programmes for students from around the world. Its new Winter Chapter takes place in Zhangjiang Science City, Shanghai's innovation hub, combining HKU-designed academic content with tech-company visits and cultural exchange.

Winter 2027 offers 'Happiness by Design: The Psychology of Wellbeing' (24–31 January, for grades 10–12 / Year 11–13) and 'Global Business Leader' (24 January – 2 February, for grades 10–12 and undergraduates in Years 1–2). Both are residential and non-credit-bearing.
highlights: HKU-designed programmes in Shanghai's tech hub
Psychology or business leadership tracks
Open to international secondary and early-undergraduate students
hkusi-winter-chapter-shanghai-2027.eligibility: Secondary students in grades 10–12 (both programmes) and undergraduates in Years 1–2 (Global Business Leader), from any country, with good English.
how_to_apply: Open the HKUSI website and choose a Winter Chapter programme
Create an account in the HKUSI application system
Submit the online application and pay fees once admitted
Arrange a Chinese visa if needed
hkusi-winter-chapter-shanghai-2027.costs: Paid residential programme; fees listed on the HKUSI site.

hkust-summer-ug-research-program-2027.about:
HKUST's Summer UG Research Program lets visiting undergraduates join a faculty-led research project in science, engineering, business or humanities at one of Asia's top technology universities. Participants work in the lab for eight weeks (14 June – 6 August 2027), are enrolled in a 3-credit research course, and receive an HKUST transcript sent to their home university.

Costs in 2027: application fee HKD 200, programme fee HKD 17,700 (housing in a shared on-campus room, visa, insurance, admin and activities) and tuition HKD 21,600 for 3 credits, waived for nominated exchange students from partner universities. Ask your home university whether it is an HKUST partner.
highlights: Wide range of research projects across HKUST schools
3 credits and an official HKUST transcript
Tuition waived for nominated exchange students
hkust-summer-ug-research-program-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates from universities outside HKUST; check the application page for year-of-study and English requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse the 2027 research projects list
Ask your home university if it can nominate you as an exchange student (tuition waiver)
Submit the online application and pay the HKD 200 fee
Arrange your Hong Kong student visa once admitted
hkust-summer-ug-research-program-2027.costs: Application fee HKD 200; programme fee HKD 17,700 (housing, visa, insurance, admin, activities); tuition HKD 21,600 (3 credits), waived for nominated exchange students.
